experiments.title: Reference operation, normal conditions
experiments.hypothesis: With reference inflows the existing hydro-dominated fleet serves demand without shortage, using the interconnector for both imports and exports.
experiments.configuration: 8760 h hourly, existing fleet, reference weather year
experiments.finding: Demand 8.00 TWh is fully served (ENS 0 MWh). Hydro supplies 6.77 TWh; gross imports 2.00 TWh and exports 1.23 TWh (net 0.77 TWh). Annual operating cost 40.8 MEUR.
experiments.limitations: Synthetic demand and prices; exports are priced at 85% of the synthetic import price.

experiments.title: Hydropower reduction under drought
experiments.hypothesis: Drought is absorbed mainly through higher net imports and cost; shortages do not occur while the interconnector is fully available.
experiments.finding: Net imports rise from 0.77 TWh (normal) to 2.26 (moderate) and 3.48 TWh (severe); operating cost rises from 40.8 to 192.7 and 324.5 MEUR/yr. ENS: 0 and 0 MWh.
experiments.limitations: Drought modelled as a uniform inflow scaling of one reconstructed year.

experiments.title: Solar without batteries
experiments.hypothesis: Import reduction per added MW of PV declines with PV size (diminishing returns).
experiments.configuration: PV +500/+1000/+1500 MW, annual hourly, normal and severe
experiments.finding: Gross import reduction per added MW: normal +500 MW: 1074 MWh/MW, +1000 MW: 898 MWh/MW, +1500 MW: 699 MWh/MW; severe +500 MW: 1406 MWh/MW, +1000 MW: 1253 MWh/MW, +1500 MW: 1022 MWh/MW. PV curtailment at +1500 MW: normal 21 GWh, severe 2 GWh.
experiments.limitations: Export capacity and the export price ratio determine how much midday PV surplus is absorbed; both are assumptions.

experiments.title: Batteries without new renewables
experiments.hypothesis: Battery operating value is modest relative to its annualised cost when reservoir hydro already provides flexibility.
experiments.finding: Annual operating saving (MEUR/yr) normal: 800 MWh: 5.5, 1600 MWh: 9.8, 3200 MWh: 13.8; severe: 800 MWh: 7.0, 1600 MWh: 12.7, 3200 MWh: 17.9. Annualised cost (MEUR/yr): 800 MWh: 25.8, 1600 MWh: 51.7, 3200 MWh: 103.3.
experiments.limitations: No ancillary-service, reserve or capacity revenues are modelled; these are often the main value streams of batteries.

experiments.title: Coordinated solar, wind, hydro and storage
experiments.hypothesis: PV and storage are complements (positive synergy in operating savings).
experiments.finding: normal: PV-only saving 135.4, battery-only 9.8, combined 146.9 MEUR/yr (synergy +1.75); severe_drought: PV-only saving 141.7, battery-only 12.7, combined 156.1 MEUR/yr (synergy +1.82)
experiments.limitations: Synergy depends on the export price ratio and NTC, both assumed.

experiments.title: Import price shock and interconnector derating
experiments.hypothesis: Price shocks raise cost but not shortage; shortages need a loss of import availability.
experiments.configuration: severe drought; price ×1–3; NTC availability 100–25% with +8% demand
experiments.finding: Annual cost rises from 324 to 968 MEUR/yr as import prices triple, with ENS 0 MWh. Unserved energy appears at NTC availability ≤ 50% (310.7 GWh).
experiments.limitations: Import availability is an exogenous scenario parameter, not a regional market model.

experiments.title: Demand growth stress test
experiments.hypothesis: Shortage grows non-linearly with demand when import availability is halved.
experiments.configuration: severe drought; demand +0–30%; NTC availability 100% and 50%
experiments.limitations: No demand response or emergency imports are modelled.

experiments.title: Investment planning under capital constraints
experiments.hypothesis: Under a binding budget the optimiser invests first in the technology with the highest operating value per euro of capital.
experiments.configuration: deterministic, normal scenario, 8 representative weeks, budgets 0–2000 MEUR
experiments.finding: Optimal additions by budget: 0 MEUR → PV 0, wind 0 MW, battery 0 MW/0 MWh; 100 MEUR → PV 126, wind 0 MW, battery 0 MW/0 MWh; 250 MEUR → PV 315, wind 0 MW, battery 0 MW/0 MWh; 500 MEUR → PV 629, wind 0 MW, battery 0 MW/0 MWh; 750 MEUR → PV 944, wind 0 MW, battery 0 MW/0 MWh; 1000 MEUR → PV 1258, wind 0 MW, battery 0 MW/0 MWh; 1500 MEUR → PV 1888, wind 0 MW, battery 0 MW/0 MWh; 2000 MEUR → PV 2000, wind 0 MW, battery 0 MW/0 MWh.
experiments.limitations: Results depend on the cost assumptions and on representative-week sampling.

experiments.title: Deterministic versus stochastic planning
experiments.hypothesis: A stochastic, risk-aware plan reduces expected cost and tail risk relative to planning for normal conditions.
experiments.configuration: 5 scenarios, 8 weeks, budget 500 MEUR, CVaR α=0.9, λ=1
experiments.finding: Risk-adjusted VSS = 0.0 MEUR/yr. The stochastic plan costs +0.0 MEUR/yr in expected cost (price of risk aversion) and lowers CVaR(0.9) of operating cost from 397.3 to 397.3 MEUR/yr. Stochastic additions: pv 629, wind 0, bp 0, be 0; deterministic (normal-year) additions: pv 629, wind 0, bp 0, be 0.
experiments.limitations: Scenario probabilities are partly assumed; five scenarios cannot represent the full distribution of climate outcomes.

experiments.title: Marginal value of flexibility
experiments.hypothesis: Dual values coincide with finite-difference marginal values where the LP is non-degenerate.
experiments.configuration: fixed base fleet, annual hourly, ± increments
experiments.finding: Severe drought, kEUR per unit-year (Δ+ / dual / Δ−): battery_energy: 3.1 / 3.3 / 4.1; battery_power: 15.5 / 18.6 / 20.3; solar_pv: 145.6 / 145.8 / 146.1; wind: 99.2 / 99.3 / n/a; import_capacity: 7.5 / 9.3 / 11.2; reservoir_volume: 0.0 / 0.0 / 0.0.
experiments.limitations: Local values around one fleet; not valid for large capacity changes.

experiments.title: When stochastic planning changes the decision
experiments.hypothesis: With restricted exports, storage/hedging value becomes scenario-dependent and the stochastic plan differs from the deterministic plan (VSS > 0).
experiments.configuration: export capacity 300 vs 900 MW; budgets 1000/1500 MEUR; λ = 0, 1
experiments.finding: With export capacity 300 MW, budget 1500 MEUR and λ=1 the stochastic plan adds pv 1520, wind 230, bp 30, be 66 vs deterministic pv 1232, wind 0, bp 0, be 0; risk-adjusted VSS 71.5 MEUR/yr; CVaR(0.9) 292 → 213 MEUR/yr for +7.8 MEUR/yr expected cost. Full-year chronology: CVaR 282.7 → 208.2 MEUR/yr for +15.1 MEUR/yr expected cost. With 900 MW export capacity VSS = 0.00 MEUR/yr.
experiments.limitations: Two export levels and two budgets only; probabilities partly assumed.

experiments.title: Representative weeks vs full-year chronology
experiments.hypothesis: Strategy rankings from the 8-week representative-period model agree with full-year chronological evaluation.
experiments.configuration: 7 plans × 5 scenarios, 8760 h hourly, fixed fleets
experiments.finding: Absolute difference in expected total cost: 1.7–10.0 MEUR/yr. Ranking (chronological): S_budget_1500, F_robust, R_l0.0_b500, B_solar, A_baseline, C_wind, D_battery; (representative weeks): S_budget_1500, B_solar, F_robust, R_l0.0_b500, A_baseline, C_wind, D_battery.
experiments.limitations: Chronological runs use V_T = V_0 per scenario year; the representative-week model uses boundaries from the existing fleet.

experiments.title: Temporal-resolution sensitivity
experiments.hypothesis: Coarser time steps understate the operating value of short-duration storage.
experiments.configuration: battery 400 MW/1600 MWh, normal year, Δt = 1, 2, 3, 6 h
experiments.finding: Battery operating saving (MEUR/yr): 1 h: 9.8, 2 h: 8.8, 3 h: 7.0, 6 h: 1.3.
experiments.limitations: One battery size and one scenario.
